subject: biology

moments.title: Fleming and penicillin
moments.body: Fleming notices mould kills bacteria on a contaminated plate. He nearly throws the plate away. Florey, Chain and Heatley turn it into a usable drug a decade later.
moments.takeaway: The accidental discovery that launches modern medicine.

moments.title: First resistance
moments.body: Even before penicillin is widely deployed, an enzyme (penicillinase) is identified that breaks down penicillin. Resistance is intrinsic to bacterial populations.
moments.takeaway: Resistance precedes wide drug use — it just gets selected by it.

moments.title: MRSA
moments.body: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is identified within a year of methicillin's introduction. MRSA spreads globally; hospital-acquired infections rise.
moments.takeaway: Bacteria evolve resistance to new drugs in months.

moments.title: Plasmid-borne colistin resistance
moments.body: mcr-1, a plasmid-borne colistin resistance gene, is found globally within months of identification. Colistin is the last-resort antibiotic against MDR Gram-negatives.
moments.takeaway: Resistance now spreads via mobile genetic elements at planetary scale.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: AMR is projected to cause 10 million deaths/year by 2050. The antibiotic pipeline is thin. Phage therapy, bacteriocins and microbiome modulation are being explored.
now.open_questions: Can we develop antibiotics faster than bacteria evolve resistance?

reflection: Fleming warned about overuse of penicillin in his 1945 Nobel lecture. The warning was ignored. Why do we so often ignore foundational warnings?
